errors.text: The hypothesis assigns peak embrittlement to ordering and percolation of B2 domains, whereas the target mediator is enhanced L12 ordering within FCC domains coupled to jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries.

It omits the essential phase-boundary mechanism: dislocation pile-ups and stress concentration at jagged boundary tips, followed by formation of ductile transition zones during high-temperature recovery.

The cited dislocation evidence concerns lattice-friction effects in chemically complex nanowires and irradiation alloys, not elevated antiphase-boundary energy, restricted cross-slip, and planar slip in ordered domains.

The proposed temperature boundary is vague and shifted from the target window of approximately 550–750 degrees Celsius, with peak embrittlement near 600 degrees Celsius and recovery near 750 degrees Celsius.
